note:
R95 - gen7 team-chant selection evidence (R90 / T-CHANT-1 follow-up). Distinguishes name presence / bank reference / reachable
selection logic / selection input / proven binding, offline, on X360 NHL 15 and PS3 NHL 15 (+ X360 NHL 10 as an era control).

Measured here:
  L1 loader: `audio/na_en_loadfile.xml` `AemsCrowdTeamChantBank` assets carry `descr="<id>"` = the bank number (same pattern as
     `AemsSfxGoalHornBank`) -> the LOADING key of a chant bank is a numeric id, i.e. the same id space as `exhibitionarena.chantaudioid`
     (R78 / R85 listing); which arena field the engine passes is not observable offline (stated).
  L2 `aemscrwd.csi` (`AemsCrowdEventDefinition`): parsed with the R20 MOIR reader - is it a NAME TABLE ONLY (table end == first string
     pointer, string pool end == EOF), i.e. no compiled body at all? (R90 called it "the compiled crowd module" - tested here.)
  L3 where else do the club picker names / keys occur? (a) as strings in any loose `.abk` / `.csi` / `.xml` / `.big`-free file of the
     tree's audio directory; (b) as their u16 name keys (low 16 bits of the bank-tree name word, R94) inside every loose bank's tree
     region (crowds.abk, controlCenter.abk, ... - a message reference by key would show up there); (c) as their MOIR ids inside the
     other `.csi` name tables.
  L4 inside a club bank: who OWNS the sample list (the club `_msg` picker or the generic `streamInterruptRecieve_msg`)? The generic
     banks (R89 §3) hang their samples off `streamInterruptRecieve_msg`. If the club list is owned by `<club>SamplePicker_msg`, playing
     it requires that message to be sent by something outside the bank; if by the generic message, a loaded club bank plays through
     the generic path.
  L5 counterexample: the Finnish arena's `chantaudioid` 61 (R90) - under L1 it LOADS `061_chant.abk` (Linköping) at that arena; the
     smallest runtime observation is therefore that arena, not an SHL club's home game (T-CHANT-1 rev. 2 proposed in the handoff).
Usage: python r95_crowd_script.py <out.json>
